newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slips on physical sales.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slips on physical sales.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were weaker at midday on Tuesday on unexpectedly aggressive physical sales by two oil majors late Monday, traders said.
"The market is weaker because of yesterday's offer by two majors. But fundamentals are strong," one trader said.
Two majors each sold 150,000 barrels of gas oil each to a Thai and a Kuwaiti trader at $32.50 a barrel for January 14-18 loading on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
January gas oil was last quoted at $32.00/$32.10 a barrel, down from Monday's $32.15/$32.25, one broker said.
The softer prices were attributed primarily to the new offers of physical gas oil in Singapore although China is still being counted on to buy record volumes in the first quarter, traders said.
The market did not pick up from the firmer prices seen in the West where February Brent crude closed up 27 cents to $23.69 per barrel.
Gas oil futures also traded firmer on London's International Petroleum Exchange, with January rising $6.00 to close at $223.00 per tonne.
Jet fuel was steady with the January jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was last quoted at $2.10/$2.40 per barrel.

Naphtha, lacking direction with Japan on a week-long holiday, was notionally quoted firmer in line with the higher crude values. January was last seen at $24.60/$24.80 a barrel, up about 10 cents from Monday.
Fuel oil was quoted unchanged at $121.25/$122.00 per tonne in quiet trade.
